paper.title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents
paper.central_claim: Pre-trained LLMs can decompose high-level household tasks into mid-level plans without training; a frozen-model inference procedure (semantic translation to admissible actions + step-wise autoregressive correction + retrieval of the most similar demonstration) raises VirtualHome plan executability from about 18% to 79% at a measurable cost in human-judged correctness.

status_reason: full text with appendix A.1-A.5 read; in-scope but borderline (plan-level LLM harness for a simulated household humanoid agent; no low-level control, no observation loop)

evidence.support_explanation: operation 1: semantic translation of generated phrases to the admissible action set

evidence.support_explanation: operation 2: step-wise interleave; the translated action conditions later steps

evidence.quote: we propose to select the most similar task T and its example plan E from the demonstration set to be used as the example in the prompt
evidence.support_explanation: operation 3: retrieval-selected one-shot example

scope_note: borderline: embodied agent in VirtualHome with LLM + external admissible-action projection (harness-like), but plan is open-loop and low-level controller is assumed; kept in scope because LLM planning with an action gate for an embodied simulator is the object of the radar's interface/verification cards

signatures.object: Planner-LM output stream for VirtualHome: free-form step phrases mapped to the 47,522-step admissible bank (42 atomic actions x allowed arguments)
signatures.information: task name + one example plan in natural-language templates; no observation, no environment feedback, no gradients; admissible action bank enumerated offline
signatures.operation: sample k single-step phrases from Planning LM; score each admissible action a_e by cosine(Translation-LM embedding) + beta * mean token log-prob; append argmax to prompt; repeat
signatures.output: sequence of admissible actions (executable VirtualHome program)
signatures.conditions: action space enumerable; one instance per object class; low-level controller assumed
signatures.feedback: none from environment; only embedding similarity score
signatures.selection_rule: argmax over a_e of max_a C + beta*P; early termination if best score < epsilon or >50% zero-length samples
signatures.selection_data: no data; epsilon/beta/k/temperature grid-searched on the 88 evaluation tasks (E013, E027)
signatures.persistence: none across tasks; translated actions persist only inside the current prompt
signatures.later_use: conditions later steps of the same plan only
signatures.failure_boundary: compounded instructions mapped poorly; premature termination; expressivity limits of VirtualHome; correctness drop

signatures.object: Prompt example for the Planning LM
signatures.information: 204-task demonstration set with plans (the 88 evaluation tasks excluded)
signatures.operation: embed task names with the Translation LM; pick the nearest demonstration; prepend as the single example
signatures.conditions: a demo set covering similar tasks
signatures.selection_rule: max cosine similarity of task names
signatures.failure_boundary: no analysis of coverage/similarity sensitivity of the demo set

retention_trace.reason: static inference-time planning procedure; no candidate-change selection or persisted harness state across tasks (demo set is fixed input)

gap.author_gap: plans produced naively by LLMs often cannot map precisely to admissible actions; prior work needed explicit step-by-step supervision
gap.checked_gap: confirmed by the paper's own Table 1: vanilla GPT-3 175B executability 7.79%, Codex 12B 18.07% (E007, E009); bottleneck is grounding of free-form output, with smaller models only appearing executable by copying the prompt example (E021)

ancestors: supervised VirtualHome program synthesis (Puig et al.; LSTM, LCS 34% with step-by-step instructions)

closest_adjacent.item: Li et al. concurrent GPT-2 fine-tuning in VirtualHome
SayCan 2204.01691v2 (concurrent, grounds by value functions, real robot)
closest_adjacent.note: cites this paper as Huang et al. and treats it as the Generative baseline

lineage.method_note: closeness judged only from pinned local texts; no external search performed, so absence of other neighbors is not evidence of novelty

gap.residue: executability gain is bought with a correctness drop (Codex 64.87->54.88); no observation or failure feedback; mid-level grounding only; evaluation set doubles as hyperparameter-selection set
gap.stakes: whether LLM world knowledge can be turned into executable embodied plans without domain training
gap.method_response: translation+step-wise correction directly targets inadmissible output; dynamic example targets environment-specific assumptions (e.g. ordering pizza)
gap.remaining_gap: correct and executable plans remain far below humans (Fig. 4 text: gap to 65.91%); grounding to sensorimotor level and environment state is explicitly left out (E014, E015)
unresolved: whether the approach transfers beyond VirtualHome (untested)
pretraining contamination of GPT-3/Codex with VirtualHome-style plans (not discussed)

assessment.evidence_level_reason: plans are generated open-loop; executability is a simulator precondition check and correctness is crowd judgment of plan text; no task-success measured by execution (EVIDENCE: offline = plan text scoring / static action accuracy)
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In VirtualHome, with frozen Codex/GPT-3 and no training, a translation-projected, step-wise, retrieval-prompted procedure makes plans far more executable (about 18->79 and 8->73) at a measured loss of human-judged correctness
assessment.author_claim_kept: extracting actionable knowledge for embodied agents without training
assessment.reproduction: all numbers are author-reported; nothing was run by us

G.reason: specific, sourced bottleneck (inadmissible free-form output) with nearest neighbors named (supervised VirtualHome work, concurrent fine-tuned GPT-2) and honest residue (correctness drop, mid-level only); SayCan-style value grounding and observation feedback are absent so the nearest-neighbor comparison is incomplete

M.reason: each operation targets a named failure (non-admissible phrasing, compounded steps, ambiguity of environment conventions) and ablation/embedding-choice results give distinguishable predictions; assumptions (enumerable action set, single instance per class, low-level controller) are stated but the soft-similarity check is only a weak proxy for validity

X.reason: Algorithm 1, templates (A.4), grids (A.1) and prompts make the chain reconstructable; conditions and failure boundary (compound instructions, premature stop, no observation, no controller) are explicit; no persistence/selection to trace; beta/epsilon values chosen on the evaluation tasks

measurement.reason: executability has an environment-defined verifier and complete denominators (88 tasks x 7 scenes); correctness uses 10 raters with SEM and a human-plan reference; metrics are matched to the plan-level claim. Not closed-loop task success (that is carried by evidence_level=offline, not double-counted); LCS is an imperfect proxy; per-task numbers not shown

causality.reason: leave-one-out ablations, Translation-LM swap (GloVe 46.92 vs SBERT/RoBERTa 73-79), program-length control and the repeat-the-example diagnostic address shortcuts; correctness not reported for ablations; fine-tuned GPT-3 13B is competitive on LCS and executability 66%

holdout.reason: 88 tasks are held out from the demo set, but the best run and sampling hyperparameters are selected by score on those same tasks and all scenes are the same simulator; no unseen environment, no pretraining-overlap audit

statistics.reason: denominators are given and correctness has SEM across annotators, fixed-example baselines average three prompts; executability has no variance/CI and failure analysis is qualitative

cost.reason: only a qualitative 'minor computation overhead'; no call/token/latency counts, though all methods share the same one-sample protocol and hyperparameter grid
